key_insight: Non-dimensionalization strongly affects buoyancy-flow PINN training: free-fall scaling avoids the severe coefficient-induced gradient imbalance observed with thermal-diffusive scaling.
engineering_relevance: Choosing an appropriate physical scaling can improve PINN heat-transfer predictions without relying on additional supervision or adaptive loss weighting.
method: Compare thermal-diffusive and free-fall scalings under identical training conditions.
Test a differentially heated square cavity at Pr = 0.71 and Ra = 10^3–10^5.
Directly measure loss gradients to assess imbalance associated with the buoyancy coefficient.
evidence_signal: For Ra ≤ 10^4, free-fall scaling yields mean Nusselt-number errors below 1.1%, versus 157–650% with diffusive scaling, which also diverges at Ra = 10^5.
watch_item: Accurate long-time heat transfer does not guarantee transient fidelity: the free-fall PINN misses the transient Nusselt-number overshoot.
paper_title: Inherent Failure Modes of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Buoyancy-Driven Flow: Role of Non-Dimensionalization in Network Training
